extracted.intended_audience: CVPR 2025 authors and reviewers (computer vision research community)
extracted.subtask_description: Conference-level rules and expectations governing submission limits, reviewer obligations and conduct, LLM usage, profile completion, data sharing, and enforcement procedures for CVPR 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors obliged to act as reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: If they do not serve in another capacity for the organization of CVPR 2025, all authors are obliged to act as reviewers. The Program Chairs (PCs) will ensure that only qualified authors have papers assigned, and the number of reviews will depend on the level of seniority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: authors who serve in another organizing capacity for CVPR 2025 or as General/Program Chairs for ICCV 2025 are exempt. ADDENDUM: Some authors of multidisciplinary papers may not be from the field of computer vision and pattern recognition; these authors will not have to commit to reviewing. Other exceptions include parental leave and military service. The number of reviews assigned to each author will be commensurate with that author’s level of contribution to CVPR 2025 submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct expectation: fair, thoughtful, and timely reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: It is expected that reviewers will submit fair and thoughtful reviews on time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general expectation motivating other enforcement mechanisms (flags, oversight). Reviews should be substantive, relevant to the paper, and submitted by deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highly irresponsible review flag (AC flagging policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Area Chairs (ACs) will have an option to flag a review as 'highly irresponsible' in addition to the prior 'not met expectations' flag. ACs will be directed to use this flag sparingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example cases of highly irresponsible behaviors: one-sentence reviews, reviews generated by Large Language Models (LLMs), reviews not relevant to the paper, or reviews that miss a substantial portion of the paper. The flag is NOT intended for reviewers who merely have misunderstandings, missed small parts of the paper, or hold a different opinion from other reviewers or the area chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oversight process and potential desk rejection for flagged or missing reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer fails to submit their reviews, or a review is flagged as being highly irresponsible, it will enter an oversight process adjudicated by the PCs. The final decision about desk rejection will be decided at the discretion of the PCs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The oversight process determines whether the review behavior merits sanction; one possible sanction is desk rejection of the papers submitted by the reviewer. This applies both to missing reviews and to reviews flagged as highly irresponsible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ban on LLMs for writing reviews and meta-reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Large language models (LLMs) are NOT allowed to be used for writing the reviews nor the meta-reviews at any step. You cannot use an LLM to write your review. This is true for any LLM, whether you run it locally or use an API.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy includes but is not restricted to: you can’t ask an LLM to write content for you (the review needs to be based on your own judgment); you can’t share substantial content from the paper or your review with an LLM (for example, you cannot use an LLM to translate a review). Permitted uses: you can use an LLM to do background research or to check short phrases for clarity. Enforcement: (Senior) ACs will check (meta-)reviews for LLM policy violations. If a review is flagged as a possible violation it will enter the same oversight process described above. The oversight will not attempt to prove LLM authorship, but will determine if the review is 'highly irresponsible'; if so, PCs may desk reject the reviewer’s papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author submission limit (max 25 papers)
rubrics_metrics.description: An author cannot submit more than 25 papers. If an author submits more than 25 papers, the Program Chairs (PCs) will desk-reject the papers registered after the twenty-fifth one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation: each author listed on a paper should make a significant and meaningful contribution to the work. The limit is intended to be ample for authors to submit their scientific contributions while preventing excessive submission counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenReview profile completion requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All the authors must complete their OpenReview profiles. Papers whose authors have not completed their profile will be desk rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: complete OpenReview profiles are required for better assignment and conflict detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer name visibility (proposed then withdrawn)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal: The reviewers’ names would be visible on OpenReview to the other reviewers of the paper after the final paper decisions have been made (to avoid authority bias). Names would also be visible to ACs, Senior ACs and PCs, as has been the policy in past years. Decision: The PCs decided not to apply this policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasoning given for withdrawing the policy: to prevent authors from discovering reviewers' identities and to protect reviewers of rejected papers. This entry records the proposed change and the final decision not to implement it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing data sharing with future venue PCs
rubrics_metrics.description: To improve future review quality, the CVPR 2025 PCs plan to share the CVPR 2025 reviewing data privately with the PCs of other future related venues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shared data will include personally identifiable records on each reviewer, including statistics on review assessments and lateness. The stated purpose is to improve future review quality; no further privacy/retention/consent details are provided on this page.
